newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to prepare inflation cut plan by end-April.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to prepare inflation cut plan by end-April.

text.p: Hungary will work out by the end of April a programme for the reduction of inflation in the next few years, a government spokesman said on Sunday.

"The government decided that the Finance Minister, also drawing the chairman of the National Bank of Hungary in the work, should work out a programme by the end of April about the reduction of the inflation rate," Elemer Kiss, Secretary of State of the Prime Minister's Office told a news conference.
Kiss added that the programme will deal with anti-inflation fight planned for the years following 1997.
Hungary's inflation is running at 18.9 percent year-on-year. Average inflation was 23.6 percent in 1996.
According to the three-year economic guidelines approved by the government last year, Hungary planned to cut inflation by five percentage points every year between 1997 and 1999.

But urged by the International Monetary Fund for a more drastic reduction, the Finance Ministry said one month ago that it would prepare alternative draft budgets for 1998, with one of them targeting a larger-than-five-percent cut.

The government and the central bank said that inflation may go down to single-digit figures in 1998 as the state of the economy did not justify high rates but the rising of the consumer index was boosted by high inflation expectations.
Analysts and officials of both the Finance Ministry and the central bank agreed that the condition of a drastic inflation cut in 1998 was a wide framework of wage and price agreements.
Analysts believe that the government will be in a difficult position if it wants to make people accept low wage increase rates for 1998, a year when Hungary will hold general elections.
